categories.name: Prompt Injection & Agent Security
categories.summary: A dominant theme this period with multiple research papers and tools addressing prompt injection vulnerabilities in LLM agents. Key findings include how clarification-seeking behaviors amplify injection success rates, supply chain risks from 'payload-less' skills that bypass static scanners, and the inadequacy of simple data/instruction separation. New defensive tooling emerged for MCP tool poisoning detection and interactive security labs.

key_items.title: MCP Prompt Injection Detector
key_items.detail: Explainable ML system using hybrid embeddings and XGBoost to flag tool-poisoning or prompt-injection content before MCP tool invocation.

key_items.title: LLM Threats Analysis Framework
key_items.detail: Checklist-style threat model for identifying where untrusted instructions cross trust boundaries in LLM apps and MCP tool flows.

key_items.title: ASPI: Clarification Amplifies Injection Risk
key_items.detail: Research showing prompt injection success rises sharply when agents solicit clarification input, highlighting need to gate clarification channels as distinct trust boundaries.

key_items.title: Payload-less Skills Exploit Agent Supply Chains
key_items.detail: Paper demonstrates how benign-looking skills can steer agents via natural-language compliance rules, bypassing signature detection entirely.

key_items.title: IPI-proxy for Red-Teaming Browser Agents
key_items.detail: Intercepting proxy that rewrites HTTP responses to embed injection payloads, enabling realistic testing of indirect prompt injection on production-like flows.

key_items.title: Contextual Integrity Lens for Injection Failures
key_items.detail: Research argues data/instruction separation is insufficient; proposes Contextual Integrity as evaluation framework for context-sensitive agent manipulation.

categories.name: Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities & CVEs
categories.summary: Two notable CVEs affecting AI tooling were disclosed. PydanticAI's SSRF blocklist can be bypassed using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, reinforcing that blocklist-only defenses remain brittle. AWS Kiro CLI has a critical flaw allowing unauthorized tool execution via piped stdin, emphasizing that CLI agents must treat non-interactive inputs as untrusted.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-46678: PydanticAI SSRF Bypass
key_items.detail: Cloud-metadata blocklist bypassed via IPv6 transition encoding; incomplete fix of prior CVE. Network-boundary egress enforcement recommended.

key_items.title: CVE-2026-9255: Kiro CLI Unauthorized Execution
key_items.detail: Missing input-source validation lets piped stdin bypass authorization prompts, enabling shell execution without user approval.

categories.name: AI-Assisted Vulnerability Research
categories.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing update reveals Claude Mythos Preview has helped uncover over 10,000 high/critical vulnerabilities in essential software within one month. This signals a paradigm shift in vulnerability discovery speed, with Anthropic advising developers to shorten patch cycles accordingly. CERT.PL also published on autonomous fuzzing capabilities.

key_items.title: Claude Mythos Finds 10K+ Critical Vulns
key_items.detail: Anthropic's unreleased frontier model has accelerated vulnerability discovery dramatically, prompting calls for faster patch cycles across the industry.

key_items.title: Project Glasswing Initial Update
key_items.detail: Anthropic's official research update on their AI-assisted security research initiative.

key_items.title: CERT.PL on Autonomous Fuzzing
key_items.detail: Technical post exploring autonomous fuzzing techniques leveraging AI capabilities.

categories.name: Agent Credential & Access Management
categories.summary: Two items address the critical challenge of secure credential handling for AI agents. Credential brokering patterns keep long-lived secrets out of model context by issuing short-lived, policy-scoped tokens at tool boundaries. Proton Pass now offers monitored credential sharing with scoped tokens and activity visibility, though enforcement must remain at the token layer.

key_items.title: Credential Brokering for AI Agents Explained
key_items.detail: Pattern reduces prompt-injection blast radius by brokering short-lived, scoped access at tool boundaries rather than exposing secrets in context.

key_items.title: Proton Pass AI Access Tokens
key_items.detail: New feature enables scoped token delegation for vault items with activity monitoring; user-approved reasons serve as audit controls.

categories.name: Security Tools & Releases
categories.summary: PromptForage emerged as a hands-on lab environment for exercising prompt injection scenarios in controlled settings, useful for documenting attack patterns before granting tool privileges. Perplexity AI also released Bumblebee on GitHub.

key_items.title: PromptForage: Interactive Injection Lab
key_items.detail: Security lab for reproducing and documenting prompt injection patterns in a controlled test harness environment.

key_items.title: Perplexity Bumblebee Release
key_items.detail: New open-source release from Perplexity AI.

top_insights: Prompt injection research is maturing beyond simple data/instruction separation toward contextual and trust-boundary-aware defenses, with multiple papers highlighting novel attack surfaces like clarification channels and payload-less skills.
AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is accelerating dramatically—Anthropic's Claude Mythos finding 10K+ critical vulns in one month signals defenders must compress patch timelines significantly.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool security is emerging as a distinct attack surface requiring pre-invocation detection layers and threat modeling beyond traditional code scanning.
Credential management for AI agents is crystallizing around brokering patterns that enforce authorization outside the model context, treating the prompt layer as untrusted.
CLI and non-interactive agent interfaces present overlooked attack vectors where stdin/pipe inputs can bypass authorization prompts intended for human operators.
